quarterly_data.signal: Q1 (Apr-Jun 2026): net asset value a record high JPY 72.3 trillion at end-June (pro forma about JPY 58.3 trillion on latest market moves); investment gain JPY 1.8 trillion, up JPY 1.3 trillion YoY, mainly from Intel (share price surged April-June) and ByteDance fair-value gains; net income JPY 347 billion. Loan-to-value 13% (policy threshold 25%); cash position JPY 2.3 trillion, covering more than two years of bond redemptions (JPY 1.5 trillion expected). S&P revised its ratings outlook from negative to stable. Strategy: become the number one ASI platform provider across four areas - AI infrastructure, AI models (OpenAI), Arm chips, and physical AI (ABB Robotics acquisition to complete by end of the year, over 30 physical-AI portfolio companies); Masayoshi Son set a 15-year goal of NAV JPY 1,000 trillion.
quarterly_data.figure: Record NAV JPY 72.3 trillion; investment gain JPY 1.8 trillion; net income JPY 347 billion; LTV 13%

contracts.signal: OpenAI investment progressing: of the $30 billion commitment made in March for this year, $20 billion has been executed as of Q1, with the remaining $10 billion to be invested toward October - bringing total investment to $64.6 billion and ownership to 13%. Financing closed one by one, including a financing agreement using OpenAI shares ($10 billion of OpenAI). SoftBank concentrates its LLM bet on OpenAI: 'We consider them more of a partner than an investment... It's our choice to put all of our eggs in OpenAI as far as LLM is concerned.'
contracts.units: $20 billion executed + $10 billion remaining toward October

quarterly_data.signal: Product adoption per SoftBank: Codex weekly active users grew from 0.4 million in December 2025 to 10 million in July 2026 - 24 times in just seven months; combined Codex plus the newly released ChatGPT Work grew 25 times in seven months. GPT-5.6, the latest revision with enhanced agentic functionality, scored highest performance in a UC Berkeley-developed evaluation at far lower cost than other AIs. OpenAI is a latecomer in the enterprise market and it is now the key growth focus; SB OpenAI Japan (JV with SoftBank) launched PaaS (patching as a service) cybersecurity for 3,000 critical-infrastructure companies in Japan. On IPO timing SoftBank had no comment but expects OpenAI to go public eventually.
quarterly_data.figure: Codex WAU 0.4 million (Dec 2025) to 10 million (July) - 24 times in seven months; Codex + ChatGPT Work combined 25 times

quarterly_data.signal: France: announced a plan to develop five gigawatt of AI data center capacity in Hauts-de-France (announced at the Choose France Summit in June 2026 in front of President Macron). First phase: EUR 45 billion investment to deliver 3.1 gigawatt of AI data center capacity in northern France by 2031, with first sites at Dunkirk, Bouches and Bosquel; the first gigawatt Bosquel AI data center is designated a fast-track project by the French government, with one gigawatt of power secured and accelerated grid connection. France's advantage: a power-exporting country, so data centers can be powered without doubling capex on new generation plants.
quarterly_data.figure: France: 5 GW plan; phase 1 EUR 45 billion for 3.1 gigawatt by 2031; 1 GW power secured at Bosquel (fast-track)

quarterly_data.signal: US projects: PORTS Technology Campus, Pike County, Ohio - the announced 10 gigawatt large-scale data center project; discussions toward execution of a lease agreement are at the final stage, and construction is expected to start in 2026. Midland County, Texas AI data center already has a lease agreement placed with OpenAI, with construction on track for delivery. Together with Schneider, SoftBank is establishing a local supply chain for power modules in Dunkirk to accelerate data center development in France.
quarterly_data.figure: Ohio PORTS 10 gigawatt - lease discussion final stage, construction starting 2026; Texas Midland lease with OpenAI on track

quarterly_data.signal: Per SoftBank's Q1 review and Arm CFO Jason Child: Arm Q1 revenue hit a record $1.3 billion, +22% YoY, with fully diluted EPS +29% YoY (record for a first quarter); Q2 guidance midpoints $1.38 billion revenue and $0.47 EPS, both above analyst consensus. Arm AGI CPU: starts shipping in Q4 of this fiscal year; initial guide was roughly $1 billion of revenue across this fiscal year and next combined, and confirmed orders have now grown to MORE than $2 billion - revenue guidance not yet updated because of supply-chain constraints primarily around wafer capacity, with clarity on how much of the incremental billion-plus can ship expected in another quarter or two; demand expected to DOUBLE the year after (Arm fiscal 2029) as the order pipeline keeps growing. Arm-based AGI CPU saves up to $10 billion of capex per 1 gigawatt of data center capacity vs x86; Arm IP-based CPU chips are used by about 50% of leading hyperscalers (Graviton, Axion, Cobalt, Grace), and NVIDIA's agentic PC chip carries an Arm-based Grace CPU.
quarterly_data.figure: Arm Q1 revenue record $1.3 billion +22% YoY; EPS +29%; Q2 guide $1.38 billion / $0.47; AGI CPU orders more than $2 billion vs ~$1 billion initial guide
